lines.en: I tap on Chika’s name in my phone and wait for her to answer.
And, since it’s still early in the day, I figure that meeting up with her now will give her the chance to not have to monitor her instinct to always act like we’re the world’s cutest couple.
She’s been having to do a lot of that lately. And...let’s just say that I’ve been a little closer to feeling bad than I normally am after telling her to tone it down.
A break can be good for everyone.
Depending on the type of break, of course. Because I’m pretty sure if I asked Chika to take a real break, all hell would break loose.
But that’s enough iterations of the word “break” for the moment.
Here’s hoping she’s awake, I guess.
: Hey! Good morning!
: Hey. You sure seem lively for someone who probably just woke up.
: Chinami wanted waffles, so I had to run over to the store to get stuff for them.
: Stop letting her control your life. If you don’t want to make waffles, don’t make waffles. It’s as simple as that.
: Do you...have something against waffles, Sensei?
: I have something against eternal kindness. And waffles just appear to be the connection between that and you this morning.
: Do you want me to be meaner to Chinami or something?
: Who wants to be mean to Chinami?! She wants to give them a piece of her mind!
: Shush. Eat your waffles.
: Okay! I love you, big sister!
: Do you hear that? That’s who you want me to be mean to.
: I never said-
: You know what, forget it. Are you busy this morning?
: Nope!
: Sweet.
: Mhm. I guess it is pretty sweet.
: This is the part where you’re supposed to invite me over.
: Is it? I wasn’t sure if that would be moving too quickly.
: Sensei! It was a joke! Of course you can come over.
: I’m not making you waffles unless you bring more ingredients, though.
: I think I’m okay without waffles. I’ll see you soon.
: We’ll be here!
I hang up the phone and start getting ready to head to Chika’s place.
When I make it to the second half of town, I see a surprising amount of its inhabitants showing a bit more life than they normally do at this time of day.
Upon trying to come up with a reason for their sudden shift in behavior, I decide to go with the simple fact that the seasons are changing.
And that, soon enough, they’ll be wandering around in search of shade or shadows instead of fire.
Good luck, old district. I wish you the best in your endless battle against death and nature.
I step into the Chosokabe apartment to find absolutely no one.
Could it be that Chika was so torn up about me asking her to slow down that she took her sister and moved to some far away land?
And, if that’s the case, why did she invite me here? Is this all just to inconvenience me?
That bitch.
: In here, Sensei!
: The bathroom?...
: Don’t worry! It’s safe to come in.
Chinami jumps onto the bed next to me, wearing nothing but an oversized t-shirt, before gazing into my eyes with a look that essentially screams, “I am secretly evil.”
: Chinami, come on. That’s my spot.
: Chinami wants to know what your intentions are with her big sister.
: Chinami should mind her own fucking business.
: Did you just curse at Chinami?! You can’t do that!
: Go put all of your money in the swear jar!
: Do you actually have one of those things?
: Why else do you think Yumi is so poor?
: Oh crap. I can’t believe I just made that joke. I’m sorry, Yumi. If it makes you feel any better, I’m also poor.
: While big sis Chika apologizes to the air, Chinami demands that you be nicer to her in the future.
: To you? Or to your sister?
: Yes.
: Oh.
: Well, uhh...okay.
: Good.
: Chinami will give back her sister’s spot now, but she’ll be watching you...
: Sure, Chinami. And I’ll make sure to drop a coin in your swear jar the next time I have cash on me.
Chinami gets off the bed and, within a matter of seconds, Chika stops apologizing to the spirit of Yumi for calling her poor and lays down beside me.

She rests her head on my lap and talks a little about how she really doesn’t want to go into work later because of the holiday rush, and I sit there the same way I always do and pretend to be interested.
Before long, though, the conversation begins to die down and more gaps begin to form- ones even larger than the half-open bathroom door that she and her sister emerged from just a short while ago.
But I guess there have been plenty of gaps forming between us as of late.
Gaps between what we want to do and what we have to do.
Gaps between what we actually do and what we struggle to.
Gaps in our own personal mindsets as they sink further into a pit that will be near impossible to climb out of if neither one of us has climbing equipment.
Chika didn’t bring hers as she believed me to be some sort of experienced climber.
And I am.
But the truth is that I don’t even know how to use my equipment.
And, at this point, I don’t know if it’s even worth the effort to learn.
The biggest gap of all is one of consciousness as Chika passes out on my lap.
I don’t mean to, but somewhere along the line, I rest my hand on her head and begin stroking her hair.
It’s slightly damp, so I’m able to figure out that she took a bath before Chinami.
But, with that and a trip to the store...just how early did she have to wake up?
: Yes, Chinami?
: Nothing.
: Chinami is just happy you’re here.
: Big sis hasn’t been sleeping much lately. But she was able to fall asleep on you right away.
: She must really, really like you.
: Yeah. She must.
: Can Chinami tell you a secret?
: Chinami is probably going to tell me anyway, so yeah.
: Well, last night, Chinami woke up in the middle of the night because she was thirsty, but she never got out of bed.
: What a fascinating secret. Thank you, Chinami.
: No, no. You don’t understand.
: Chinami didn’t want to get out of bed because her sister was crying.
: So she just pretended to stay asleep and hugged her instead.
: Did you two get into a fight?
: Something like that.
: Does this mean you’re going to stop coming over?
: No, it doesn’t.
Not...now, at least.
I have no idea what’s going to happen in the future-
Or what other gaps will form.
: That’s good.
: Chinami likes when you’re here. And she doesn’t want to hear her sister cry anymore.
: Do you have to hear that often?
: Not really.
: Not since Mommy died.
: But Chinami thinks big sis Chika will stop crying as much if you tell her you love her.
: Or give Chinami a little sister.
: Okay, stop that.
: Chinami will convince you one day.
: If Chika had a baby, it wouldn’t even be your sister. It would be your [niece].
: Chinami would be an aunt?!
: Yes. And you’re way too young to be an aunt.
: This is a really sticky situation!
: That’s right. So, for everyone’s sake, please stop asking me to have a baby with your sister.
: Fine! But Chinami isn’t happy about it!
: Chinami seems to very rarely be happy about anything I do.
: Then make it up to her by not letting big sis cry anymore.
: Chinami can only do so much to cheer her up all alone. She needs your help.
: I’ll see what I can do...
Chinami lays down beside her sister and falls asleep as well.
Next thing I know, I’m surrounded by two lightly breathing, unconscious blondes and unable to figure out a way to escape this situation.
Not that it’s a bad one, just...not how I imagined my morning going.
But, I guess there are more ways to ensure that these two get a good night’s sleep than just buying them a brand new bed.
Or...good morning’s sleep.
I’ll just hang around here until they wake up, I guess.
Chika’s affection has increased to [chika_love]!
Chinami’s affection has increased to [chinami_love]!
Both sisters wake up a few hours later and you’re able to get on with the rest of your day...
: I would...sure hope so.
: Papa!
: Nope.
: What? What’s wrong?
: What do you mean what’s wrong? You said it was safe to come in.
: Hm? Cause of Chinami? She’s just a kid, it’s no big deal.
: It’s not like I’m giving Yumi a bath in here.
: That’s exactly why it’s a problem. I would have stayed inside without a question if Yumi was in there.
: Hey. Watch it.
: Why won’t Papa come inside? Is he afraid of the bath?
: I guess he just hates you, Chinami.
: I don’t-
: Papa, why?!
Am I really the weird one for thinking the right thing to do is wait out here?
I get that Chika’s comfortable enough with me that she doesn’t feel threatened about me being around...that.
But why would I even go in there if I can just talk to them through the gap in the door?
: Stop being so sketchy and come in already. I’ve just gotta get the soap out of her hair.
: Chinami misses you! And you should want to spend time with her because no one knows how much time she has left!
: Chinami! Stop saying that! I mean it!
: Yes, big Sister...
: Do it again and I’m taking your phone away. That’s not funny.
What...should I do here?
Wait outside
: If you’re almost done, I’ll just wait out here.
: There’s really no need for me to be in there right now anyway.
: Not sure why you’re being so weird about this, but okay. Do whatever makes you comfortable, I guess.
I avert my gaze as I make my way into the combined living room and bedroom, collapsing onto the same worn down mattress these sisters so often fall asleep on together.
And as I wait for the two of them to finish in the bathroom, I’m stricken by the unhealthy thought that I now want to buy them a new bed in addition to their phones.
Maybe this is just one more way I can trick myself into thinking I’m somehow a positive influence on their lives...but maybe it’s more than that?
Maybe I do actually want to help them? Or...give them better lives or something.
Or maybe that’s just me imagining a single trace of light in a world I believe to be devoid of it.
You can’t give someone a better life by just handing them things they’d have trouble obtaining on their own.
Sure, it would make things a little better for them in the moment, but what comes after that?
Chika’s already starting to depend on me a little too much.
But I guess it would be hard not to depend on me when I’m the first person in a long time that’s actually felt dependable.
It’s sad.
I thought she was smarter than this.
Go in. This is normal.
Chika’s right.
This would only be a big deal if I turned it into one.
And treating Chinami like she’s a normal girl instead of what she really is would be the number one way to do that.
In fact, Chika would probably be more suspicious if I stayed outside.
That’s right.
This is normal.
I am normal.
: Hooray! Papa doesn’t hate Chinami after all!
: You good?
: Yeah. I just thought Chinami would feel uncomfortable having a boy in here. That’s all.
: Chinami doesn’t know why that would change anything. She likes Papa and wants him to always be around.
: And Chika didn’t realize this was going to be a point of contention.
: Well, Sensei thinks it’s time to talk about something else before this gets even weirder.
: Chinami is pleased with how everyone is speaking now. She feels like she is starting a trend.
: Chinami should learn to wash her own hair instead of making her big sister do it all the time.
: And she should also take off her ribbon when she’s in the bath.
: But if Chinami takes off her ribbon, Chinami will deflate! It is what keeps all of the air inside of her! And where she stores her magic!
Just like I thought.
This is all completely normal.
: Papa, help! Chinami wants you to wash her hair instead! Big sis Chika is being too rough!
: I’m good right here, thanks.
: Want me to wash your hair next, Sensei? Tub’s already full. Might as well get as much out of the water as we can.
: Again, I’m good right here. I think that tub might be a little too small for me anyway.
: Suit yourself! Don’t come crying to me when you run up your water bill, though.
: The water bill is a mostly negligible cost once you aren’t confined to working a minimum wage retail job anymore.
: Oh yeah? Wanna help me go look for a new one, then? You know, since you’re already helping Yumi and whatnot.
: Big sis Yumi will never get a job. She’s too misunderstood.
: You’d certainly be easier to find one for.
: I think you should be fine where you are until you’re out of school, though. If you can’t find a new job after that, then I’ll help you go hunting.
: Yumi’s just getting all the special treatment then, huh? Job hunting and bath company.
: Hey, I never would have offered to watch her if you didn’t bring the idea up.
: Well, I’ll be sure to relay it to her the next time she goes to wash her hair.
: Please don’t. She hates me enough as is. The last thing I need is her knowing that I’m getting myself involved in conversations like this.
: Chinami thinks big sis Yumi likes you a lot and that she just doesn’t know how to express it!
: She always says she never had a mom or a dad, so Chinami thinks that she never learned how to be nice.
: If somebody teaches big sis Yumi to be nice, Chinami thinks she’ll start saying less mean things to you.
: Why don’t you teach her to be nice, Chinami?
: Chinami tries! But big sis Yumi has already tried to kill her once!
: Is this about the peanuts?
: It’s about the peanuts.
: Nowhere is safe for Chinami! This is a dog eat dog world, and Chinami is a dog sometimes!
: Yeah, yeah. How about we just both try to teach Yumi how to be nice, then?
: Just not too nice. Because then Papa might think twice about coming over here to see me.
: Hey, I’m here for Chinami. You’re just a bonus.
: Uh-huh. Right. So you just dialed my number by mistake this morning?
: Your numbers are right next to each other in my phone. I probably just tapped the wrong one.
: Be careful, big sister! It looks like you might really have to worry after all!
: Hey! Shh! I told you not to talk about that! I wasn’t “worrying” about anything! I was just...thinking!
: Chinami can’t be stopped! And she can’t help if Papa likes her more than her big sister!
: Worrying?
: About what we talked about at the mall?
: Um...could you give the two of us a minute, Sensei? I’d like to remind my sister about certain things I don’t want her saying around you.
: Please?
: Sure. Though, it is a little weird to be kicked out of this room when you practically begged me to come inside.
: I wouldn’t say I begged...
: I would.
Especially since it helps me justify how long I just hung around my fake girlfriend’s naked sister for.
As I leave the room, though, I realize that I was just making a big deal over nothing-
And that just seeing someone without their clothes on isn’t enough for me to want them.
I’m not used to that.
I’m not used to feeling like I’m in complete control over how I feel because, frankly, most of the time, I’m not.
I’m glad that today I was, though.
And I hope that, at least for a while longer-
I will continue to be.
I make my way into the combined living room and bedroom, collapsing onto the same worn down mattress the Chosokabe sisters so often fall asleep on together.
And as I wait for the two of them to finish in the bathroom, I’m stricken by the unhealthy thought that I now want to buy them a new bed in addition to their phones.
Maybe this is just one more way I can trick myself into thinking I’m somehow a positive influence on their lives...but maybe it’s more than that?
Maybe I do actually want to help them? Or...give them better lives or something.
Or maybe that’s just me imagining a single trace of light in a world I believe to be devoid of it.
You can’t give someone a better life by just handing them things they’d have trouble obtaining on their own.
Sure, it would make things a little better for them in the moment, but what comes after that?
Chika’s already starting to depend on me a little too much.
But I guess it would be hard not to be when I’m the first person in a long time that’s actually felt dependable.
It’s sad.
I always thought she was smarter than this.
